name: Field Doctor-Style Chicken Tagine (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
600 g Chicken
350 g Whole grain rice
3/4 x 400 g tins Plum Tomato
1 1/4 medium Sweet Potatoes
1 medium Courgette
175 g Spinach
1 1/4 Red Peppers
1 medium Carrot
85 g Red Quinoa
41 g Kalamata Olives [olives, water, salt, red wine vinegar, extra virgin olive oil]
1 1/4 tbsp Tomato Puree [tomato]
1/4 Lemon Juice
1 1/4 tsp Chicken Stock (Chicken Extract, Chicken Fat, Salt], Tamari [water, SOYA beans, sea salt], Coriander, Pumpkin Seed, Sweet Noble Paprika, Tapioca Starch, Chive, Parsley Flat, Sunflower Seed, Persian Spice Mix, Lemon Zest (0.1%), Turmeric Blend, Sea Salt
directions:
1. Grains: Cook wholegrain rice and red quinoa; drain and keep warm.

2. Brown chicken: Season chicken and brown in extra virgin olive oil; set aside.

3. Tagine: Soften courgette, red pepper, carrot and chives. Add chopped tomato, tomato puree, Persian spice mix, sweet paprika, turmeric, lemon juice, lemon zest, tamari, chicken stock and water. Return chicken with olives; simmer until chicken is cooked and sauce is thick (tapioca slurry if needed).

4. Finish: Wilt spinach into the sauce. Serve over rice–quinoa with coriander, parsley, pumpkin and sunflower seeds.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.
description:
Ingredients: Chicken, Water, Whole grain rice, Chopped Tomato, Sweet Potato, Courgette, Spinach, Red Pepper...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Chicken Tagine (Low FODMAP) (~357 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/aromatic-chicken-tagine
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~357 g x 8 = 2856 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~348 g (inferred ~12.17% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~41 g (inferred ~1.45% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
